correctness.rationale: The KKT complementarity argument yields exactly the same threshold map for all real p>1. Each full-dimensional active-set region has derivative the centering block C_k; line integration gives exact global Lipschitz modulus as the largest block norm. Riener Theorem 1.3 reduces the global symmetric quartic norm inequality to all two-level inputs; the exact two-variable Hölder norm yields every finite block formula. The rational function in q=r+r^-1 has derivative 3(-q^2+2q+2)/(q-1)^4, with unique maximum 1+2/sqrt(3). Rational splits approximate it but never attain it since the maximizing t(1-t)=(3-sqrt(3))/18 is irrational. A new standalone symbolic script verifies the critical algebra and finite witnesses; symbolic tests do not replace the all-dimensional half-degree theorem.

value.rationale: Standard simplex projection is a canonical nonexpansive Hilbert-space retraction used in probability and optimization. In real ell_4 its sharp sensitivity is not one: the theorem computes the complete finite-dimensional nonlinear stability profile and its optimal uniform sharp constant, including a strict finite-versus-asymptotic gap and all best-approximation exponents 1<p<infinity. The object and exact invariant are natural, not a selected numerical slice. A known linear hyperplane norm ingredient may overlap but does not by itself eliminate the quantitative nonlinear-retraction question.
